learning_objective: 🎯 Master the physics of liquids and gases! Learn why ships float, how airplanes fly using Bernoulli's principle, and why water rises inside narrow tubes.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Pressure in a fluid increases with depth ($P = \rho gh$). Pascal's Law states that if you apply pressure to an enclosed fluid, it is transmitted equally in every direction. This is how hydraulic lifts can raise a massive car using a tiny push!
Any object completely or partially submerged in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces. This is exactly why heavy steel ships can float.

For a flowing, ideal fluid, if the speed of the fluid increases, its internal pressure must decrease. This pressure difference creates 'Lift', which is the primary reason airplane wings can lift jets into the sky.

Viscosity is the internal friction between layers of a flowing fluid. Water has low viscosity, but honey has high viscosity. When an object falls through a viscous fluid, it eventually reaches a constant maximum speed called 'Terminal Velocity'.

Water molecules on the surface pull together tightly, acting like a stretched elastic membrane (allowing insects to walk on water). This same force pulls water UP against gravity inside very narrow glass tubes (Capillary action).

fun_activity.title: 📄 The Paper Lift
fun_activity.instructions: Hold a strip of paper just beneath your lips and blow hard OVER the top of it. Instead of blowing down, the paper will magically lift UP! Your fast-moving breath creates low pressure on top (Bernoulli's Principle), and the higher pressure below pushes the paper up.

exam_tips: 📌 The derivation of Bernoulli's Theorem using the Work-Energy theorem is one of the most important derivations in Class 11 physics.
📌 Equation of Continuity ($A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2$) explains why water shoots out faster when you partially cover the nozzle of a garden hose.
📌 Master Stokes' Law ($F = 6\pi \eta rv$) for calculating terminal velocity in a viscous medium.
quick_recap: ⭐ Pressure at a point inside a liquid is completely independent of the shape of the container.
⭐ Hot fluids are less viscous than cold fluids (which is why hot syrup pours faster).
⭐ Raindrops are perfectly spherical because surface tension tries to minimize the total surface area.
